# ACTIVITY PATTERNS

We are going to determine the independence threshold for each of the focal species: 
```{r}

labels <- c("Short (0-60)", "Long (60-120)")

delta <- Focal_species %>%
  arrange(Station, Species, DateTimeOriginal) %>%
  group_by(Station, Species) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_min = as.numeric(difftime(DateTimeOriginal,
                                    lag(DateTimeOriginal),
                                    units = "mins"))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(delta_min), delta_min > 0, delta_min <= 120) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_type = factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
        delta_min <= 60 ~ labels[1],
        delta_min > 60 & delta_min <= 120 ~ labels[2],
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = labels
    )
  )

plot_delta_species <- function(species_name, data) {
  df <- data %>% filter(Species == species_name)
  
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = paste0(species_name, " - No delta data"), size = 6) +
        theme_void() +
        ggtitle(species_name)
    )
  }
  
  if (nrow(df) < 2) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 1, y = 1, label = paste0(species_name, " - Not enough delta data"), size = 6) +
        theme_void() +
        ggtitle(species_name)
    )
  }
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = delta_min, fill = delta_type)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(~ delta_type, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") + #the plot starts where the data register starts, that's why there are some plots that start at 0 and others at 30 
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Short (0-60)" = "cyan4",
                 "Long (60-120)" = "darkblue")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = species_name,
      x = "Delta time (min)",
      y = "Density"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 13),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      aspect.ratio = 0.5
    )
}

all_species <- unique(Focal_species$Species)

plots_delta <- lapply(
  all_species,
  plot_delta_species,
  data = delta
)

names(plots_delta) <- all_species

for (sp in all_species) {
  print(plots_delta[[sp]])
}
```

We just have delta for 9 species out of 17, because they are the only ones that have a delta (as the others don't have consecutive registers)
=> As this happened, we asked Rstudio to give us a message for the species that did not have delta data: 

The result is the following: 
-> Not enough delta data: Grey himalayan goral & grey wolf
-> No delta data        : Common leopard, Himalayan black bear, golden jackal, black bear, jackal & cat

/!\ It seems to not be very clear where is the independence threshold graphically talking, so we're gonna use the 95percentiles
```{r Percentiles}
delta_short_range <- delta %>%
  filter(delta_min > 0, delta_min <= 120)
delta_short_range %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    p90 = quantile(delta_min, 0.90),
    p95 = quantile(delta_min, 0.95),
    p99 = quantile(delta_min, 0.99)
  )
```
-> the 95th percentiles of delta times ranged between 60 and 114 min across species. Based on this, we decided to follow a conservative approach in which detection separated by more than 60 minutes where considered as independent.  

We are now going to do a triage and only keep the independent registers for each species:
```{r Triage}
independent_occ <- Focal_species %>%
   arrange(Species, DateTimeOriginal) %>%
  group_by(Species) %>% #so this allows to do the following JUST between registers of the same species
  mutate(
    time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(DateTimeOriginal, lag(DateTimeOriginal), units = "mins"))) %>% #creates a timediff column with the time lapse between two registers
  filter(is.na(time_diff) | time_diff >= 60) %>% #allows to only conserve records separated by 60  or more mins 
  mutate(n_independent_records = n()) %>%   # count per species 
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    Station,
    Species,
    DateTimeOriginal,
    time_diff,
    n_independent_records
  ) %>%
  distinct(Species, .keep_all = TRUE) #keeps just a line per species 
```

We need to convert time into day fraction & h_decimal 
```{r}
#Into day fractions 
Act.pattern_data <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  mutate(day_fraction = as.numeric(Time) / 86400)

#Into radians 
Act.pattern_data <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
  mutate(radians = day_fraction * 2 * pi) # as we are working on the 24h format & should be between 0 — 6.283185
```

Now we are going to try to obtain the translape coefficient (i.e., non-parametric mesure that allows to compare activity patterns between species, sites, sex, age, periods...)

For samples < 50 --> we use the Dhat 1 and for > 75 --> Dhat 4
=> We will use the Dhat4 for all our pairs  
```{r Overlap between species}
#we are going to do this with a loop to avoid doing this manually with all the combinations possible 
rad_list <- list(
  `blue sheep` = B.sheep_rad,
  `dog`        = Dog_rad,
  `grey himalayan goral`     = G.him.gor_rad,
  `himalayan brown bear`  = Him.br.bear_rad,
  `himalayan tahr`  = Him.tahr_rad, 
  `livestock`       = Livestock_rad, 
  `musk deer`       = M.deer_rad, 
  `siberian ibex`   = S.ib_rad, 
  `snow leopard`    = S.le_rad, 
  `red fox`         = R.fox_rad
)
pairs <- combn(names(rad_list), 2, simplify = FALSE) #we generate all possible combinations
results <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  
  sp1 <- p[1]
  sp2 <- p[2]
  
  rad1 <- rad_list[[sp1]]
  rad2 <- rad_list[[sp2]]
  
  n1 <- length(rad1)
  n2 <- length(rad2)
  min_n <- min(n1, n2)
  
  # Choose estimator
  dhat_type <- ifelse(min_n < 50, "Dhat1", "Dhat4")
  
  dhat <- overlapEst(rad1, rad2, type = dhat_type)
  
  data.frame(
    species_1 = sp1,
    species_2 = sp2,
    estimator = dhat_type,
    overlap   = dhat[dhat_type],
    n1 = n1,
    n2 = n2,
    min_n = min_n
  )
})

 #we generate the loop
overlap_table <- do.call(rbind, results) #we generate a dataframe with everything in
rownames(overlap_table) <- NULL
```

We are now going to plot the overlaps between species
```{r Overlaps' plotting (between species)}
plot_overlap_pair <- function(p) { #p = my different pairs
  
  sp1 <- as.character(p[1])
  sp2 <- as.character(p[2])
  
  rad1 <- rad_list[[sp1]]
  rad2 <- rad_list[[sp2]]
  
   dhat_value <- overlap_table$overlap[
    (overlap_table$species_1 == sp1 & overlap_table$species_2 == sp2) |
    (overlap_table$species_1 == sp2 & overlap_table$species_2 == sp1)
  ] #select the overlap value (Dhat)
  
  overlapPlot(
    rad1, rad2,
    main = NULL,
    linecol = c("black", "gray40"),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    bty = "L",
    xlab = "Hour",
    ylab = "Density"
  )
  
  legend(
    "topright",
    inset = c(-0.02, -0.2), #- => upper and righter
    legend = c(sp1, sp2),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    col = c("black", "gray40"),
    bty = "n",
    xpd = TRUE  # let move the legend inside the margins
  )
  
  mtext(
  text = bquote("Dhat" == .(sprintf("%.2f", dhat_value))), # to print 2 numb after the comma
  side = 3,        
  adj = 0,         # lined at the left hand 
  line = 1.5,      # put it a little bit upper in order that it will be alined with the righ hand legend
  cex = 0.9
)#add the dhat
}

overlaps <- lapply(pairs, plot_overlap_pair) #aply to all pairs

```

Now we are going to examine overlaps for the same species but between stations 
-> Let´s start between stations with and without predators
```{r Stations with vs without predators}
Act.pattern_data <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate(Predator = ifelse(any(Species %in% c("snow leopard", 
                                               "leopard cat", 
                                               "himalayan black bear", 
                                               "common leopard", 
                                               "himalayan brown bear", 
                                               "red fox")), 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

#Let's calculate overlaps 
species_list <- names(rad_list)
results <- lapply(species_list, function(sp) {
  
  rad_pred <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Predator == 1) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  
  rad_nonpred <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Predator == 0) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  
  if (length(rad_pred) == 0 | length(rad_nonpred) == 0) return(NULL) # has to have data in at least one condition
  
  n1 <- length(rad_pred)
  n2 <- length(rad_nonpred)
  min_n <- min(n1, n2)
  
  dhat_type <- if(min_n < 50) "Dhat1" else "Dhat4"
  dhat      <- overlapEst(rad_pred, rad_nonpred)
  
  data.frame(
    species   = sp,
    estimator = dhat_type,
    overlap   = dhat[dhat_type],
    n_pred    = n1,
    n_nonpred = n2,
    min_n     = min_n
  )
})

overlap_pred_vs_nonpred <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), results))
rownames(overlap_pred_vs_nonpred) <- NULL

#Let's plot them 
plot_overlap_predator <- function(sp) {
  
  rad_pred <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Predator == 1) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  
  rad_nonpred <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Predator == 0) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  
  if (length(rad_pred) == 0 | length(rad_nonpred) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  # Extraer el dhat value desde el dataframe ya calculado
  dhat_value <- overlap_pred_vs_nonpred$overlap[
    overlap_pred_vs_nonpred$species == sp
  ]
  
  overlapPlot(
    rad_pred, rad_nonpred,
    main    = sp,
    linecol = c("black", "gray40"),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    bty = "L",
    xlab = "Hour",
    ylab = "Density"
  )
  
  legend(
    "topright",
    inset  = c(-0.02, -0.2),
    legend = c("predator", "no predator"),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    col = c("black", "gray40"),
    bty = "n",
    xpd = TRUE
  )
  
  mtext(
    text = bquote("Dhat" == .(round(dhat_value, 2))),
    side = 3,
    adj  = 0,
    line = 1.5,
    cex  = 0.9
  )
}
overlaps_pred <- lapply(species_list, plot_overlap_predator)
```

```{r Stations with vs without livestock}
  )
})

overlap_livestock_vs_nonliv. <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), results))
rownames(overlap_pred_vs_nonpred) <- NULL

#Plot it
plot_overlap_livestock <- function(sp) {
  
  rad_livestock <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Livestock == 1) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  
  rad_nonlivest. <- Act.pattern_data %>% 
    filter(Species == sp, Livestock == 0) %>% 
    pull(radians)
  if(length(rad_livestock) == 0 | length(rad_nonlivest.) == 0) return (NULL)

    dhat_value <- overlap_livestock_vs_nonliv.$overlap[
     overlap_livestock_vs_nonliv.$species == sp
  ]
  
  overlapPlot(
    rad_livestock, rad_nonlivest.,
    main    = sp,
    linecol = c("black", "gray40"),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    bty = "L",
    xlab = "Hour",
    ylab = "Density"
  )
  
  legend(
    "topright",
    inset  = c(-0.02, -0.2),
    legend = c("livestock", "no livestock"),
    lty = c(1, 2),
    lwd = c(2.8, 2.8),
    col = c("black", "gray40"),
    bty = "n",
    xpd = TRUE
  )
  
  mtext(
    text = bquote("Dhat" == .(formatC(dhat_value, format = "f", digits = 2))),
    side = 3,
    adj  = 0,
    line = 1.5,
    cex  = 0.9
  )
}
```

```{r Circular activity plot, fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
circ_data <- list(B.sheep_circ, Dog_circ, G.him.gor_circ, Him.br.bear_circ, Him.tahr_circ, Livestock_circ, M.deer_circ, S.ib_circ, S.le_circ, R.fox_circ)
species_name <- c("blue sheep", "dog", "grey himalayan goral", "himalayan brown bear", "himalayan tahr", "livestock", "musk deer", "siberian ibex", "snow leopard", "red fox")

circular_plots <- function(data_circ, species_name, shrink = 1.18, bins = 24, prop = 2) {
  plot(density.circular(data_circ, bw = 40), lwd = 2, lty = 1, main = species_name, shrink = shrink)
  points.circular(data_circ, stack = TRUE)
  rose.diag(data_circ, bins = bins, ticks = FALSE,
            prop = prop, pc = 21, border = "black",
            col = "gray", add = TRUE)
}

for(i in seq_along(circ_data)) {
  circular_plots(circ_data[[i]], species_name[i])
}

#to test dispersion/concentration of registers around the pick (it can be an appendix, as editorials are known to ask for s & s0 values instead of r)
rho_values <- sapply(circ_data, rho.circular)
activity_results <- data.frame(Species = species_name, Rho = rho_values)

#we are going to calculate the activity peak 
mean_peak <- sapply(circ_data, mean.circular, units = "hours")
peak_hours <- (mean_peak %% (2 * pi)) * 24 / (2 * pi)
peak_hms <- as_hms(round(mean_peak * 3600))

activity_results <- activity_results %>%
  mutate (Peak_hour = peak_hms)
```

Mean vector length (rho) : measures the concentration of data points around a central activity peak. A lower rho indicates a less concentrated distribution, meaning the data points are more spread out.
-> Blue sheep             : 0.12, 
-> Dog                    : 0.02, rho super low -> distribution is highly dispersed, with little concentration around the a.peak 
-> Grey himalayan goral   : 0.29, rho quite low -> a bit higher than others, BUT relatively low =>  data is not highly conc. 
-> Himalayan brown bear   : 0.09,
-> Himalayan tahr         : 0.16,
-> Livestock              : 0.06,
-> Musk deer              : 0.29, rho quite low -> a bit higher than others, BUT relatively low =>  data is not highly conc. 
-> Siberian ibex          : 0.14,
-> Snow leopard           : 0.03
-> Red fox                : 0.54

We are going to calculate the standard circular deviation (s)
```{r}
s_values <- sapply(circ_data,sd.circular)
activity_results <- activity_results %>%
  mutate (S = s_values)  
activity_results <- select(activity_results, Species, Rho, S, Peak_hour)
```
Super important dispersion for all of the focal species!!! 

To be able to determine which circular test we will use, firstly we will determine the distribution of every species activity: 
-> Blue sheep, grey himalayan goral, himalayan brown bear, himalayan tahr, musk deer & red fox: MULTIMODAL
=> Rao's test because of dispersion

-> Dog, Livestock, siberian ibex & snow leopard: UNIMODAL & lowly concentrated and highly dispersed
=> Rao's spacing test (detects uniformity deviations even with quite dispersed data )

-> We will not perform the Watson–Williams test for any of our focal species because its assumptions are violated: the circular distributions are not all approximately von Mises, concentration parameters differ markedly among species, and some species exhibit nearly uniform activity patterns.
```{r Circular statistical tests}
results <- list()
for (i in 1:length(circ_data)) {
  species_data <- circ_data[[i]]
  test_result <- rao.spacing.test(species_data, alpha = 0.05)
  results[[species_name[i]]] <- test_result
}
results
```
->Activity clustering for Himalayan brown bear, Siberian ibex & Snow leopard as test value < critical value => the activity patterns of this species deviate from a uniform distribution(with the actual data we can't say there's a a clear preference for specific times, that the data suggests their activity is spread evenly throughout the day)

For the other species, the null hypothesis of uniformity was rejected, even though some  were close to the critical value. This indicates that there is insufficient evidence to conclude that the activity patterns of any species deviate from a uniform distribution(with the actual data we can't say there's a a clear preference for specific times, that the data suggests their activity is spread evenly throughout the day)

```{r Styled circular plots}
circular_plots_styled <- function(data_circ, species_name, bins = 24, prop = 2.5,
                                   bar_col = "blue4") {
  
  plot.new()
  plot.window(xlim = c(-1.7, 1.7), ylim = c(-1.7, 1.7), asp = 1)
  title(main = species_name, cex.main = 1.1)
  
  draw_sector <- function(h_start, h_end, col, r = 1.25) {
    a_start <- pi/2 - (h_start / 24) * 2 * pi
    a_end   <- pi/2 - (h_end   / 24) * 2 * pi
    if (h_end > h_start) {
      theta <- seq(a_start, a_end, length.out = 200)
    } else {
      theta <- seq(a_start, a_end - 2*pi, length.out = 200)
    }
    x <- c(0, r * cos(theta), 0)
    y <- c(0, r * sin(theta), 0)
    polygon(x, y, col = col, border = NA)
  }
  
  # Night
  draw_sector(18.9, 24, col = adjustcolor("lightcyan3", 0.9))
  draw_sector(0,5.8, col = adjustcolor("lightcyan3", 0.9))
  # Crepuscule
  draw_sector(5.8, 6.2,  col = adjustcolor("burlywood", 0.9))
  draw_sector(18.5, 19, col = adjustcolor("burlywood", 0.9))
  # Day
  draw_sector(5.8, 18.5, col = adjustcolor("bisque2", 0.85))
  
   rose.diag(data_circ,
            bins   = bins,
            ticks  = FALSE,
            axes = FALSE,
            prop   = prop,
            border = "black",
            col    = bar_col,
            add    = TRUE,    
            shrink = 0.85)
  
    r_circ <- 1.25
  theta_all <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = 500)
  lines(r_circ * cos(theta_all), r_circ * sin(theta_all),
        col = "gray30", lwd = 1.2)
  
  for (h in 0:23) {
    ang   <- pi/2 - (h / 24) * 2 * pi
    r_lbl <- 1.42
    lbl   <- if (h == 0) "0/24" else as.character(h)
    text(r_lbl * cos(ang), r_lbl * sin(ang),
         labels = lbl, cex = 0.60, col = "gray15")
    lines(c(1.22 * cos(ang), 1.28 * cos(ang)),
          c(1.22 * sin(ang), 1.28 * sin(ang)),
          col = "gray40", lwd = 0.7)
  }
  mtext("Number of records", side = 2, line = 0.5, cex = 0.7)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))  
colours <- "royalblue4"
for (i in seq_along(circ_data)) {
  circular_plots_styled(circ_data[[i]], species_name[i], bar_col = colours)
}
```

```{r GAMMs data prep}
covs_sel <- Focal_species %>%
  rename(
    NDVI        = `NDVI (5km)`,
    Temperature = `Mean temperature`
  ) %>%
  select(Station, Altitude, NDVI, Temperature) %>%
  distinct()

  left_join(covs_sel, by = c("Station", "Species"))
```

```{r GAM dog effect}
library(mgcv)
library(activity)
#see Bollen et al., 2024 & to go further Iannarilli et al.,2024

# ====================== Goral =================================================
G.him.goral <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  filter(Species == "grey himalayan goral") %>%
  mutate(
    Dog     = factor(Dog, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    Station = factor(Station),
    season  = factor(season)
  )

dog_effort_goral <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  mutate(
    Dog     = factor(Dog, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    season  = factor(season),
    Station = factor(Station)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Station, season, Dog) %>%
  summarise(
    dog_effort = n_distinct(Date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

dog_effort_goral

Foraggregation_goral <- G.him.goral %>%
  distinct(Station, Dog, season)

G.him.goral_agg <- Foraggregation_goral %>%
  crossing(hour_bin = 0:23) %>%
  left_join(
    G.him.goral %>%
      mutate(hour_bin = floor(h_decimal)) %>%
      group_by(Station, Dog, season, hour_bin) %>%
      summarise(n_detections = n(), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Station", "Dog", "season", "hour_bin")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi
  ) %>%
  left_join(dog_effort_goral, by = c("Station", "Dog", "season"))

GAMM_dog <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Dog +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  #cc, cylcic cubic bcs we are working on the diel cycle, which is circular
    s(radians, by = Dog, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(Station, bs = "re") + # re, cause aleatory effect
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(dog_effort)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = G.him.goral_agg,
  method = "fREML", # = to Restricted Maximum Likelihood
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

gam.check(GAMM_dog)
#QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD 
# Resids. vs linear pred: Fan pattern => maybe use bn instead of poisson?
#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson 
#response vs fitted values => GOOD

    offset(log(dog_effort)),

  data = deer_dog_agg,

  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

GAMM_dogdeer_nb <- bam(

)
```

```{r GAMM livestock effect}
#============ Blue sheep =======================================================
B.sheep <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  filter(Species == "blue sheep") %>%
  mutate(
    Livestock     = factor(Livestock, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    Station = factor(Station),
    season  = factor(season)
  )

livestock_effort_sheep <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  mutate(
    Livestock = factor(Livestock, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    season  = factor(season),
    Station = factor(Station)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Station, season, Livestock) %>%
  summarise(
    livestock_effort = n_distinct(Date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Foraggregation_B.sheep <- B.sheep %>%
  distinct(Station, Livestock, season)

B.sheep_agg <- Foraggregation_B.sheep %>%
  crossing(hour_bin = 0:23) %>%
  left_join(
    B.sheep %>%
      mutate(hour_bin = floor(h_decimal)) %>%
      group_by(Station, Livestock, season, hour_bin) %>%
      summarise(n_detections = n(), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Station", "Livestock", "season", "hour_bin")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi
  ) %>%
  left_join(livestock_effort_sheep, by = c("Station", "Livestock", "season"))
GAMM_sheep_livestock <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  #cc, cylcic cubic bcs we are working on the diel cycle, which is circular
    s(radians, by = Livestock, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(Station, bs = "re") + # re, cause aleatory effect
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(livestock_effort)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = B.sheep_agg,
  method = "fREML", # = to Restricted Maximum Likelihood
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

gam.check(GAMM_sheep_livestock)
#K ->1 => 0.99 = good signal capture & p>0.5 no need for more nodes 
#QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD 
# Resids. vs linear pred: Fan pattern => maybe use bn instead of poisson?
#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson 
#response vs fitted values => GOOD 
GAMM_sheep_livestock_nb <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(radians, by = Livestock, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(Station, bs = "re") +
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(livestock_effort)),
  family = nb(),
  data = B.sheep_agg,
  method = "fREML",
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)
gam.check(GAMM_sheep_livestock_nb)
AIC(GAMM_sheep_livestock, GAMM_sheep_livestock_nb)
#AIC =1.. not real difference, more parsimonious?

sum(residuals(GAMM_sheep_livestock, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(GAMM_sheep_livestock)
mean(B.sheep_agg$n_detections == 0)
# no overdispersion 

mu_hat <- fitted(GAMM_sheep_livestock)
prop_zeros_the_poisson <- mean(dpois(0, lambda = mu_hat))
prop_zeros_obs <- mean(B.sheep_agg$n_detections == 0)

c(obs = prop_zeros_obs, teor = prop_zeros_the_poisson)
#obs more or less 0 to theor => we can keep Poisson

#CONFUNDANT EFFECT BETWEEN LIVESTOCK AND STATION!!!!! => check if difFerence between groups 
table(B.sheep_agg$season, B.sheep_agg$Livestock)

B.sheep_covs <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  filter(Species == "blue sheep") %>%
  mutate(
    Livestock     = factor(Livestock, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    Station = factor(Station),

    Altitude = Altitude,
    NDVI = NDVI,
    Temperature = Temperature
    )

covs_livestock <- B.sheep_covs %>%

# Welch Two Sample t-test
t.test(Temperature ~ Livestock, data = covs_livestock)
#no difference of temperature between sites => comparables
t.test(Altitude ~ Livestock, data = covs_livestock)
#no difference of altitude between sites => comparables
t.test(NDVI ~ Livestock, data = covs_livestock)
# no difference of altitude between sites => comparables

GAMM_livestock_sheep_simp <- gam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
                 s(radians, k=10) + 
                 s(radians, by=Livestock, k=5) +
                 s(season, bs="re"),
  family = poisson(),
  data = B.sheep_agg,
  method = "REML"
)
gam.check(GAMM_livestock_sheep_simp)
## k -> 1 => 0.99 = good signal capture & p > 0.5, no need for more knots
# QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD
# Resids. vs linear pred: V-shaped pattern, expected for ZIP models 
#                         with high proportion of structural zeros (92.6%) => GOOD
# Histogram of residuals: 2 peaks, not ideal but expected due to the 
#                         large amount of structural zeros => GOOD
# Response vs fitted values: model underestimates high counts, expected 
#                            given the low number of real detections (n=57),
#                            but captures zero-inflation adequately => ACCEPTABLE
summary(GAMM_livestock_sheep_simp)

    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  #cc, cylcic cubic bcs we are working on the diel cycle, which is circular
    s(radians, by = Livestock, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(Station, bs = "re") + # re, cause aleatory effect
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(livestock_effort)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = Goral_agg,
  method = "fREML", # = to Restricted Maximum Likelihood
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

gam.check(GAMM_goral_livestock)
#K ->1 => 0.99 = good signal capture & p>0.5 no need for more nodes 
#QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD 
# Resids. vs linear pred: Fan pattern => maybe use bn instead of poisson?
#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson 
#response vs fitted values => GOOD 

sum(residuals(GAMM_goral_livestock, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(GAMM_goral_livestock)
mean(Goral_agg$n_detections == 0)
#Oversdispersion, 0.37 more than perfect dispersion for Poisson moderated

mu_hat <- fitted(GAMM_goral_livestock)
prop_zeros_the_poisson <- mean(dpois(0, lambda = mu_hat))
prop_zeros_obs <- mean(B.sheep_agg$n_detections == 0)

c(obs = prop_zeros_obs, teor = prop_zeros_the_poisson)
sum(residuals(GAMM_livestock_sheep_simp, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(GAMM_livestock_sheep_simp)
#obs more or less 0 to theor => we can keep Poisson

# var < mean = SUBDISPERSION => => No need of ZINB ... so just ZIP 
GAMM_goral_livestock_zip <- gam(
  list(
    n_detections ~ s(radians, k=10) + 
                   s(radians, by=Livestock, k=10) +
                   s(Station, bs="re") + 
                   s(season, bs="re"),
      ~ s(radians, k=10) + 
      s(Station, bs="re")
  ),
  family = ziplss(),
  data = Goral_agg,
  method = "fREML"
)
AIC(GAMM_goral_livestock_zip, GAMM_goral_livestock)
## k -> 1 => 0.99 = good signal capture & p > 0.5, no need for more knots
# QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD
# Resids. vs linear pred: pattern expected for ZIP models 
#                         with high proportion of structural zeros (87%) => GOOD
# Histogram of residuals: asymetrical => OK
# Response vs fitted values: model slightly underestimates high counts likely due to higher number of real detections => ACCEPTABLE
summary(GAMM_goral_livestock_zip)

  ) %>%

Goral_agg_LIVESTGORAL$Livestock <- factor(Goral_agg_LIVESTGORAL$Livestock,

#How many wt/wtt livestock ?
 Goral_agg_LIVESTGORAL %>% filter(n_detections > 0) %>% count(Livestock)
# 5wtt vs 53 with => 
 
GAMM_summer_only <- gam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
                 s(radians, bs="cc", k=10) + 
                 s(radians, by=Livestock, k=10),
  family = poisson(),
  data = Goral_agg_LIVESTGORAL %>% filter(season == "summer"),
  method = "REML"
)
summary(GAMM_summer_only)
 # compareCkern
goral_livestock_absent <- Goral$h_decimal[Goral$Livestock == "absent"] * 2 * pi / 24
goral_livestock_present <- Goral$h_decimal[Goral$Livestock == "present"] * 2 * pi / 24
fit_absent <- fitact(goral_livestock_absent)
fit_present <- fitact(goral_livestock_present)
compareCkern(fit_absent, fit_present, reps = 1000)

# GAM ZIP failed to detect a significant effect of livestock on goral diel activity (p > 0.05), likely due to the low number of detections in livestock-absent stations (n = 96 sampling occasions, mostly zeros) and complete confounding with station identity.
# However, compareCkern confirmed significantly different activity patterns between conditions (p = 0.024), supported by low temporal overlap (Dhat = 0.36).

#Watson test
absent_circ <- circular(Goral$h_decimal[Goral$Livestock == "absent"] * 2 * pi / 24,
                        type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

present_circ <- circular(Goral$h_decimal[Goral$Livestock == "present"] * 2 * pi / 24,
                         type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

watson.two.test(absent_circ, present_circ)
# Watson's two-sample test: 0.01 < p < 0.05) confimed that goral substantially modify their activity timing in the presence of livestock. The GAM ZIP failed to detect this effect due to complete confounding between livestock presence and station identity in the sampling design.

# Predict 
newdata_goralLIVEST <- expand.grid(
  hour_bin = seq(0, 23.99, length.out = 200),
  Livestock = factor(c("absent", "present"),
                     levels = levels(Goral_agg_LIVESTGORAL$Livestock))
) %>%
  mutate(
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi
  )

pred_goralLIVEST <- predict(
  GAMM_summer_only,
  newdata = newdata_goralLIVEST,
  type = "response",
  se.fit = TRUE
)

newdata_goralLIVEST <- newdata_goralLIVEST %>%
  mutate(
    fit = pred_goralLIVEST$fit,
    se  = pred_goralLIVEST$se.fit,
    fit_lwr = pmax(fit - 1.96 * se, 0),
    fit_upr = fit + 1.96 * se
  )


predictplot_livestgoral <- ggplot(newdata_goralLIVEST, aes(x = hour_bin, y = fit, color = Livestock, fill = Livestock)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = fit_lwr, ymax = fit_upr), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("absent" = "cyan4", "present" = "purple4")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("absent" = "cyan4", "present" = "slateblue")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1.6, 0.2),expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Hour of the day", y = "Predicted activity density", color = "Livestock", fill = "Livestock") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.90, 0.90),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )

ggsave(predictplot_livestgoral, file = "Predict Livestock-goral.png", dpi = 1000)

s.ibex_livestock <- Act.pattern_data %>%

Foraggregation_ibexlivestock <- s.ibex_livestock %>%

ibex_livestock_agg <- Foraggregation_ibexlivestock %>%
  crossing(hour_bin = 0:23) %>%
  left_join(
    s.ibex_livestock %>%
      mutate(hour_bin = floor(h_decimal)) %>%
      group_by(Station, Livestock, season, hour_bin) %>%
      summarise(n_detections = n(), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Station", "Livestock", "season", "hour_bin")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi
  ) %>%
  left_join(livestock_effort_goral, by = c("Station", "Livestock", "season"))
ibex_livestock_agg$Livestock <- factor(ibex_livestock_agg$Livestock, levels = c("absent", "present"))

ibex_livestock_agg <- ibex_livestock_agg %>%
  mutate(
    Station = factor(Station),
    season  = factor(season)
  )

GAMM_livestockibex <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  
    s(radians, by = Livestock, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(livestock_effort)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = ibex_livestock_agg,
  method = "fREML", 
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

gam.check(GAMM_livestockibex)
#QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD 
# Resids. vs linear pred: Fan pattern => maybe use bn instead of poisson?
#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson 
#response vs fitted values => GOOD 
GAMM_livestockibex_nb <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Livestock +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(radians, by = Livestock, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(livestock_effort)),
  family = nb(),
  data = ibex_livestock_agg,
  method = "fREML",
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)
gam.check(GAMM_livestockibex_nb)
AIC(GAMM_livestockibex, GAMM_livestockibex_nb)
#real difference, more parsimonious (Nb)

    )

ibex_covs <- Act.pattern_data %>%

Foraggregation_ibexlivestock <- s.ibex_livestock %>%

ibex_agg_LIVEST <- Foraggregation_ibexlivestock %>%
  crossing(hour_bin = 0:23) %>%
  left_join(
    s.ibex_livestock %>%
      mutate(hour_bin = floor(h_decimal)) %>%
      group_by(Station, Livestock, season, hour_bin) %>%

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),

  ) %>%

ibex_agg_LIVEST$Livestock <- factor(ibex_agg_LIVEST$Livestock, 
                                        levels = c("absent", "present"))

                                           levels = c("summer", "winter"))

GAMM_summer_only_ibexL <- gam(
         n_detections ~ Livestock +
           s(radians, bs="cc", k=10) + 
             s(radians, by=Livestock, k=10),
     family = nb(),
     data = ibex_agg_LIVEST %>% filter(season == "summer"),
     method = "fREML"
 )
summary(GAMM_summer_only_ibexL)

# compareCkern
ibex_livestock_absent <- s.ibex_livestock$h_decimal[s.ibex_livestock$Livestock == "absent"] * 2 * pi / 24
ibex_livestock_present <- s.ibex_livestock$h_decimal[s.ibex_livestock$Livestock == "present"] * 2 * pi / 24
fit_absent <- fitact(ibex_livestock_absent)
fit_present <- fitact(ibex_livestock_present)
compareCkern(fit_absent, fit_present, reps = 1000)

#Watson test

                        type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

                         type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

 exclude = c("s(livestock_effort)", "s(season)", "s(NDVI)")
)

newdata_ibexlivestock <- newdata_ibexlivestock %>%
```

```{r GAMM predator effect}
B.sheepPRED <- Act.pattern_data %>%

SheepPRED_agg <- Foraggregation_sheepPRED %>%

  ) %>%

    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),

  left_join(covs_sheepPRED, by = "Station")


#cONFUNDANT EFFFECT? 
table(SheepPRED_agg$Station, SheepPRED_agg$Predator)

table(SheepPRED_agg$season, SheepPRED_agg$Predator)
#season does not

# Welch Two Sample t-test

GAMM_sheepPRED <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Predator +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  #cc, cylcic cubic bcs we are working on the diel cycle, which is circular
    s(radians, by = Predator, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(season, bs = "re"),
  family = poisson(),

  method = "REML", #

)

#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson

sum(residuals(GAMM_sheepPRED, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(GAMM_sheepPRED)
mean(SheepPRED_agg$n_detections == 0)

prop_zeros_the_poisson <- mean(dpois(0, lambda = mu_hat))

c(obs = prop_zeros_obs, teor = prop_zeros_the_poisson)

# ======== Tahr ================================================================
H.tahr_PRED <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  filter(Species == "himalayan tahr") %>%
  mutate(
    Predator     = factor(Predator, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    Station = factor(Station),
    season  = factor(season)
  )

predator_effort_tahr <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  mutate(
    Predator     = factor(Predator, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    season  = factor(season),
    Station = factor(Station)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Station, season, Predator) %>%
  summarise(
    predator_effort = n_distinct(Date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Foraggregation_tahrPRED <- H.tahr_PRED %>%
  distinct(Station, Predator, season)

tahrPRED_agg <- Foraggregation_tahrPRED %>%
  crossing(hour_bin = 0:23) %>%
  left_join(
    H.tahr_PRED %>%
      mutate(hour_bin = floor(h_decimal)) %>%
      group_by(Station, Predator, season, hour_bin) %>%
      summarise(n_detections = n(), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Station", "Predator", "season", "hour_bin")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_detections = replace_na(n_detections, 0),
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi
  ) %>%
  left_join(predator_effort_tahr, by = c("Station", "Predator", "season"))

GAMM_tahrpredator <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Predator +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +  
    s(radians, by = Predator, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(predator_effort)),
  family = poisson(),
  data = tahrPRED_agg,
  method = "fREML", 
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)

gam.check(GAMM_tahrpredator)
#QQ-PLOT: deviance residuals aligned to diagonal => GOOD 
# Resids. vs linear pred: Fan pattern => maybe use bn instead of poisson?
#histogramm of residuals: asymetrical distibution, but expected with Poisson 
#response vs fitted values => GOOD 
GAMM_tahrpredator_nb <- bam(
  n_detections ~ Predator +
    s(radians, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(radians, by = Predator, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
    s(season, bs = "re") +
    offset(log(predator_effort)),
  family = nb(),
  data = tahrPRED_agg,
  method = "fREML",
  knots = list(radians = c(0, 2 * pi))
)
gam.check(GAMM_tahrpredator_nb)
AIC(GAMM_tahrpredator, GAMM_tahrpredator_nb)
#AIC  real difference, more parsimonious (nb)

table(tahrPRED_agg$Predator)
table(tahrPRED_agg$Station, tahrPRED_agg$Predator)
#CONFUNDANT EFFECT BETWEEN DOG AND STATION!!!!! 

# => check if difFerence between groups 
tahrPRED_covs <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  filter(Species == "himalayan tahr") %>%
  mutate(
    Predator     = factor(Predator, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("absent", "present")),
    Station = factor(Station),
    season  = factor(season), 
    Altitude = Altitude,
    NDVI = NDVI,
    Temperature = Temperature
    )

covs_tahrpredator <- tahrPRED_covs %>%
  distinct(Station, Predator, Altitude, NDVI, Temperature,Predator)

# Welch Two Sample t-test
t.test(Temperature ~ Predator, data = covs_tahrpredator)
#no difference of temperature between sites => comparable
t.test(Altitude ~ Predator, data = covs_tahrpredator)
#no difference of altitude between sites => comparable
t.test(NDVI ~ Predator, data = covs_tahrpredator)
#no difference of NDVI between sites => comparable
table(tahrPRED_agg$season, tahrPRED_agg$Predator) 
#No confundant effect of season

summary(GAMM_tahrpredator_nb)

# compareCkern
tahr_predator_absent <- H.tahr_PRED$h_decimal[H.tahr_PRED$Predator == "absent"] * 2 * pi / 24
tahr_predator_present <- H.tahr_PRED$h_decimal[H.tahr_PRED$Predator == "present"] * 2 * pi / 24
fit_absent <- fitact(tahr_predator_absent)
fit_present <- fitact(tahr_predator_present)
compareCkern(fit_absent, fit_present, reps = 1000)

#Watson test
absent_circ <- circular(H.tahr_PRED$h_decimal[H.tahr_PRED$Predator == "absent"] * 2 * pi / 24,
                        type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

present_circ <- circular(H.tahr_PRED$h_decimal[H.tahr_PRED$Predator == "present"] * 2 * pi / 24,
                         type = "angles", units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")

watson.two.test(absent_circ, present_circ)

# Predict 
newdata_tahrPRED<- expand.grid(
  hour_bin = seq(0, 23.99, length.out = 200),
  Predator = factor(c("absent", "present"), levels = levels(tahrPRED_agg$Predator))
) %>%
  mutate(
    radians = (hour_bin + 0.5) / 24 * 2 * pi,
    NDVI = mean(tahrPRED_agg$NDVI, na.rm = TRUE),
    season = tahrPRED_agg$season[1],
    predator_effort = 1
  )

pred_tahrPRED <- predict(
  GAMM_tahrpredator_nb,
  newdata = newdata_tahrPRED,
  type = "response",
  se.fit = TRUE,
  exclude = "s(predator_effort)"
)

newdata_tahrPRED <- newdata_tahrPRED %>%
  mutate(
    fit = pred_tahrPRED$fit,
    se  = pred_tahrPRED$se.fit,
    fit_lwr = pmax(fit - 1.96 * se, 0),
    fit_upr = fit + 1.96 * se
  )

predictplot_predatortahr <- ggplot(newdata_tahrPRED, aes(x = hour_bin, y = fit, color = Predator, fill = Predator)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = fit_lwr, ymax = fit_upr), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("absent" = "cyan4", "present" = "purple4")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("absent" = "cyan4", "present" = "slateblue")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.1, 0.02), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Hour of the day", y = "Predicted activity density", color = "Predator", fill = "Predator") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.90, 0.90),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )

ggsave(predictplot_predatortahr, file = "Predict Predator-tahr.png", dpi = 1000)

  labs(x = "Hour of the day", y = "Predicted activity density", color = "Predator", fill = "Predator") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.90, 0.90),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black")
  )

ggsave(predictplot_predatoribex, file = "Predict Predator-ibex.png", dpi = 1000)
```

```{r}
global_presence_matrix <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  select(Station, Species) %>%
  distinct() %>%                        
  mutate(presence = 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Species,
    values_from = presence,
    values_fill = 0                     
  )
```

```{r}
weekly_presence_matrix <- Act.pattern_data %>%
  mutate(
    Year = year(Date),
    Week = isoweek(Date) #the ISO week is a standar form of week, starting on Mondays, etc.
  ) %>%
  select(Station, Year, Week, Species) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(presence = 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Species,
    values_from = presence,
    values_fill = 0
  )
```

```{r}
species_cols <- c("dog", "livestock", "snow leopard", "siberian ibex",
                  "red fox", "himalayan brown bear", "grey himalayan goral",
                  "musk deer", "blue sheep", "himalayan tahr")

weekly_presence_matrix$Station <- tolower(weekly_presence_matrix$Station)
weekly_presence_matrix <- weekly_presence_matrix %>% filter(!Station %in% c("dodhganga top", "hurling nalllah", "after chandra taal", "batal", "chota dhara nala", "gyundi nalla 2", "anzabari 2", "habbakhatoon top", "mimarg ridge", "niril rdg", "dodh halan", "geem 1_full"))
weekly_presence_matrix <-  weekly_presence_matrix%>%
  mutate(Station = ifelse(Station == "darkhond top", "darkhund top", Station))

sites    <- unique(weekly_presence_matrix$Station)
nSites   <- length(sites)
nSpecies <- length(species_cols)

nOcc <- max(table(weekly_presence_matrix$Station))
nOcc  # site with the highest number of occurences per week 

z <- array(0, dim = c(nSites, nSpecies, nOcc)) # cosntruct array z (sites*species*occurrence) => to make an estimation of the detection probability for each species 
for (i in seq_along(sites)) {
  site_data <- weekly_presence_matrix %>% filter(Station == sites[i])
  n_visits  <- nrow(site_data)
  
  for (k in seq_along(species_cols)) {
    z[i, k, 1:n_visits] <- site_data[[species_cols[k]]]
  }
}

```

```{r Covariates for MSOMs}
Focal_species <- Focal_species %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate(Predator = ifelse(any(Species %in% c("snow leopard", 
                                               "leopard cat", 
                                               "himalayan black bear", 
                                               "common leopard", 
                                               "himalayan brown bear", 
                                               "red fox")), 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()
Focal_species <- Focal_species %>% 
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate (Dog = ifelse(any(Species %in% "dog"), 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

Focal_species <- Focal_species %>% 
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate (Livestock = ifelse(any(Species %in% "livestock"), 1, 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

sites <- tolower(sites)

Cov_MSOMs <- data.frame(Station = sites) %>%
  left_join(
    Focal_species %>%
      select(Station, Locality, Altitude, `NDVI (5km)`, `Mean temperature`, Predator, Dog, Livestock) %>%
      distinct(Station, .keep_all = TRUE),
    by = "Station"
  ) 

Cov_MSOMs[!complete.cases(Cov_MSOMs), ] #to see where are NAs
Cov_MSOMs <- Cov_MSOMs %>% filter(!Station %in% c("dodhganga top", "hurling nalllah", "after chandra taal", "batal", "chota dhara nala", "gyundi nalla 2", "anzabari 2", "habbakhatoon top", "mimarg ridge", "niril rdg", "dodh halan", "geem 1_full")) #drop these stations
Cov_MSOMs <- Cov_MSOMs %>%
  mutate(Station = ifelse(Station == "darkhond top", "darkhund top", Station))
Cov_MSOMs <- Cov_MSOMs %>%
  filter(!(Station == "darkhund top" & is.na(Altitude)))
Cov_MSOMs[!complete.cases(Cov_MSOMs), ]
```

```{r Strong overlap}
species_pair0 <- c("dog", "livestock")
species_pair1 <- c("siberian ibex", "dog")
species_pair2 <- c("blue sheep", "dog")
species_pair3 <- c("blue sheep", "livestock")

idx_pair0 <- which(species_cols %in% species_pair0)
idx_pair1 <- which(species_cols %in% species_pair1)
idx_pair2 <- which(species_cols %in% species_pair2)
idx_pair3 <- which(species_cols %in% species_pair3) #to be able to select each species

get_detection_matrix <- function(z, species_idx) {
  matrix(z[, species_idx, ], nrow = nSites, ncol = nOcc)
}

det_list_pair0 <- list(
  dog           = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair0[1]),
  livestock = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair0[2])
)

det_list_pair1 <- list(
  dog           = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair1[1]),
  siberian_ibex = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair1[2])
)

det_list_pair2 <- list(
  dog        = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair2[1]),
  blue_sheep = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair2[2])
)

det_list_pair3 <- list(
  livestock  = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair3[1]),
  blue_sheep = get_detection_matrix(z, idx_pair3[2])
) # Matrixes per pair

umf_pair0 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair0)
umf_pair1 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair1)
umf_pair2 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair2)
umf_pair3 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair3) # Creates unmarkedFrames

## Null MSOMs (without interactions)
m_null_pair0 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "0"),
  data = umf_pair0
)

m_null_pair1 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "0"),
  data = umf_pair1
)

m_null_pair2 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "0"),
  data = umf_pair2
)

m_null_pair3 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "0"),
  data = umf_pair3
)

## MSOMs (with interactions)
m_inter_pair0 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "~1"),
  data = umf_pair0
)

m_inter_pair1 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "~1"),
  data = umf_pair1
)

m_inter_pair2 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "~1"),
  data = umf_pair2
)

m_inter_pair3 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~1", "~1", "~1"),
  data = umf_pair3
)

##Lets compare models 
modSel(fitList(
  null       = m_null_pair0,
  interaction = m_inter_pair0
))

modSel(fitList(
  null       = m_null_pair1,
  interaction = m_inter_pair1
))

modSel(fitList(
  null       = m_null_pair2,
  interaction = m_inter_pair2
))

modSel(fitList(
  null       = m_null_pair3,
  interaction = m_inter_pair3
))
```

Lowest AIC = Interaction model

#MSOMs WITH COVARIATES

```{r Dog & Livestock}
Cov_MSOMs_std <- Cov_MSOMs %>%
  mutate(
    Altitude         = as.numeric(scale(Altitude)),
    `Mean temperature` = as.numeric(scale(`Mean temperature`)),
    `NDVI (5km)`     = as.numeric(scale(`NDVI (5km)`)),
    Predator         = as.numeric(scale(Predator)),
    Dog              = as.numeric(scale(Dog)),
    Livestock        = as.numeric(scale(Livestock))
  )

umfc_pair0 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair0, siteCovs = Cov_MSOMs_std)

#Model choice (Authomatic selection through AIC (as dredge is not compatible with this types of models we use this loop) 
covs <- c("Altitude", "`Mean temperature`", "`NDVI (5km)`", "Predator")

grid <- expand.grid(replicate(length(covs), c(TRUE, FALSE), simplify = FALSE))
colnames(grid) <- covs

results <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(grid)) {
  
  selected <- covs[as.logical(grid[i, ])]
  
  formula_str <- if (length(selected) == 0) "~1" else paste("~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))
  
  model_name <- if (length(selected) == 0) "null" else paste(gsub("`", "", selected), collapse = " + ")
  
  tryCatch({
    m <- occuMulti(
      detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
      stateformulas = c(formula_str, formula_str, "~1"),
      data = umfc_pair0
    )
    results[[model_name]] <- data.frame(
      Model    = model_name,
      Formula  = formula_str,
      AIC      = m@AIC,
      nParams  = length(coef(m))
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Did not converged: ", model_name)
  })
}

aic_table <- do.call(rbind, results)
aic_table <- aic_table[order(aic_table$AIC), ]
aic_table$deltaAIC <- round(aic_table$AIC - min(aic_table$AIC), 3)
aic_table$weight   <- round(exp(-0.5 * aic_table$deltaAIC) / 
                            sum(exp(-0.5 * aic_table$deltaAIC)), 3)
rownames(aic_table) <- NULL
aic_table
#we choose the model that has altitude, mean temperature and predators based on the AIC table. ... We selected the best-ranked model based on AIC (ΔAIC = 0), as the difference with the second model was negligible (ΔAIC < 2)

m_inter_cov_pair0 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~Altitude + `Mean temperature` +  Predator ",
                    "~Altitude +  `Mean temperature` + Predator ",
                    "~1"),
  data = umfc_pair0
)

m_inter_COV_pair0 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~Altitude + `Mean temperature` +  Predator ",
                    "~Altitude +  `Mean temperature` + Predator ",
                    "~`Mean temperature` + Predator"),
  data = umfc_pair0
)
summary(m_inter_cov_pair0)
summary(m_inter_COV_pair0)
m_inter_COV_pair0@AIC
m_inter_cov_pair0@AIC#no sign. effects of covariates on the interaction
```

```{r Dog & Siberian ibex}
umfc_pair1 <- unmarkedFrameOccuMulti(y = det_list_pair1, siteCovs = Cov_MSOMs_std)
#Model choice 
covs <- c("Altitude", "`Mean temperature`", "`NDVI (5km)`", "Predator", "Livestock")

grid <- expand.grid(replicate(length(covs), c(TRUE, FALSE), simplify = FALSE))
colnames(grid) <- covs

results <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(grid)) {
  
  selected <- covs[as.logical(grid[i, ])]
  
  formula_str <- if (length(selected) == 0) "~1" else paste("~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))
  
  model_name <- if (length(selected) == 0) "null" else paste(gsub("`", "", selected), collapse = " + ")
  
  tryCatch({
    m <- occuMulti(
      detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
      stateformulas = c(formula_str, formula_str, "~0"),
      data = umfc_pair1
    )
    results[[model_name]] <- data.frame(
      Model    = model_name,
      Formula  = formula_str,
      AIC      = m@AIC,
      nParams  = length(coef(m))
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Did not converged: ", model_name)
  })
}
aic_table_1 <- do.call(rbind, results)
aic_table_1 <- aic_table_1[order(aic_table_1$AIC), ]
aic_table_1$deltaAIC <- round(aic_table_1$AIC - min(aic_table_1$AIC), 3)
aic_table_1$weight   <- round(exp(-0.5 * aic_table_1$deltaAIC) /
                            sum(exp(-0.5 * aic_table_1$deltaAIC)), 3)
rownames(aic_table_1) <- NULL
aic_table_1 #we choose the model that has l altitude, ivestock, mean temperature and predators based on the AIC table.
#Now we are going to see if it is worth it to add the dog covaiate for the siberian ibex 

m_wtt_dog <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~0"),
  data = umfc_pair1
)

m_wt_dog <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~ `Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock + Dog",
                    "~0"),
  data = umfc_pair1
)

modSel(fitList(
  dog        = m_wtt_dog,
  no_dog     = m_wt_dog
))
#The inclusion of dog as a covariate for Siberian ibex did improve model fit (ΔAIC = 0.29), and was therefore included

m_null_cov_pair1 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~ `Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~`Mean temperature` + Predator + Livestock + Dog",
                    "~0"),                  # interaction term, intercept only
  data = umfc_pair1
)
summary(m_null_cov_pair1)
```

```{r Dog & Blue sheep}
m_wtt_dog <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator + Livestock + Dog",
                    "~0"),
  data = umfc_pair2
)

m_wt_dog <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~ Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~0"),
  data = umfc_pair2
)

modSel(fitList(
  dog        = m_wtt_dog,
  no_dog     = m_wt_dog
)) #we keep the model without dog, cause it has the lowest AIC, highest AICweight and is the most parciomonious.
#DeltaAIC = 0.54 < 2, so both models are competitive, but we prefer the simpler model when the difference is negligible.

m_null_cov_pair2 <- occuMulti(
  detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
  stateformulas = c("~Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator ",
                    "~Altitude + `Mean temperature` + `NDVI (5km)` + Predator + Livestock",
                    "~0"),                  # interaction term, intercept only
  data = umfc_pair2
)
```

```{r Grey himalayan goral & dog}
  model_name <- if (length(selected) == 0) "null" else paste(gsub("`", "", selected), collapse = " + ")
  
  tryCatch({
    m <- occuMulti(
      detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
      stateformulas = c(formula_str, formula_str, "~1"),
      data = umfc_list_new[[9]]
    )
    results[[model_name]] <- data.frame(
      Model    = model_name,
      Formula  = formula_str,
      AIC      = m@AIC,
      nParams  = length(coef(m))
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Did not converged: ", model_name)
  })
}
aic_table_12 <- do.call(rbind, results)
aic_table_12 <- aic_table_12[order(aic_table_12$AIC), ]
aic_table_12$deltaAIC <- round(aic_table_12$AIC - min(aic_table_12$AIC), 3)
aic_table_12$weight   <- round(exp(-0.5 * aic_table_12$deltaAIC) /
                            sum(exp(-0.5 * aic_table_12$deltaAIC)), 3)
rownames(aic_table_12) <- NULL
aic_table_12 #we choose the model that has temperature, livestock and predators

m_inter_cov_pair12 <- occuMulti(
    detformulas   = c("~1", "~1"),
     stateformulas = c("~`Mean temperature` + Livestock + Predator",
                    "~`Mean temperature` + Livestock + Predator",
                    "~1"), 
    data = umfc_list_new[[9]]
  )
m_inter_cov_pair12
```

#MODELS' VALIDATION
```{r}
fitstats <- function(mod, method = "nonparboot") {
  
  # Helper to safely flatten list-of-matrices or plain matrices
  flatten <- function(x) {
    if (is.list(x)) as.numeric(do.call(cbind, x))
    else as.numeric(x)
  }
  
  obs  <- flatten(getY(mod@data))
  exp  <- flatten(fitted(mod))
  res  <- flatten(residuals(mod, method = "nonparboot"))
  
  sse      <- sum(res^2,                        na.rm = TRUE)
  chisq    <- sum((obs - exp)^2 / exp,          na.rm = TRUE)
  freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(obs) - sqrt(exp))^2,    na.rm = TRUE)
  
  out <- c(SSE          = sse,
           Chisq        = chisq,
           freemanTukey = freeTuke)
  
  return(out)
}

#Dog & Livestock

              fitstats,
              nsim = 1000,
              method = "nonparboot")

pb

chat <- fitstats(m_inter_cov_pair0)["Chisq"] / mean(pb@t.star[,"Chisq"])
chat

par(mfrow = c(3,1))
```
